title: Vote Republican | Letters To Editor | ellsworthamerican.com
text:
To the Editor:
Vote for Susan Collins, Bobby Charles and Paul LePage.
Vote for Bobby Charles for governor. He has management experience. Big jobs and big numbers don’t bother him, and he knows how to save money without being too painful. He has contacts in Washington. He knows how to ask them for help when problems come up. His proposals to fix our problems may seem radical, but can we solve them by doing the same things over and over again as the other two candidates propose?
Vote for Paul LePage for U.S. House of Representatives. Do you remember when he became governor? He was left with a $490 million debt the state owed to hospitals. He got that paid. In Washington he’ll help the president with two things that Trump promised and voters want — cutting spending and controlling immigration.
Vote for Susan Collins for U.S. Senate. She can take a beating from various news outlets and pundits, and still stand proudly and produce results for the state of Maine.
She is blamed for overturning Roe v. Wade because Brett Kavanaugh told her it was settled law so she voted for him to be a Supreme Court judge. Was it her fault for believing him and what he thought was right at the time? She has always been pro abortion choice, a position I disagree with, but that one issue does not stop me from voting for her.
PACs are spending millions blaming Sen. Collins for President Trump's agenda, but those ads are not authorized by any candidate. Troy Jackson knows those accusations, if not lies, are taken out of context, but the damage is done and he’s smiling. If he’s elected, what will his record be? Not bipartisan I’ll bet.
Sen. Collins is endorsed by Sen. Joe Manchin, former Sen. Bill Cohen, Bill Green, the Maine Fraternal Order of Police and the Sportsman’s Alliance of Maine, which said “she fights unbelievably hard for our issues and heritage” and “earned an 'A' rating opposed to Jackson's 'F'”.
Yes, Jackson changed his mind about gun control like he did on abortion. Which way will the wind blow next?
I don’t presume that anything I write will change your mind if you have already made your choice, but if you haven’t or are thinking of not voting at all, please think and vote. The future of our state and country depends on it.
Peter Clapp
Blue Hill
